definitions.explanation: A large mass of ice that has broken off from a glacier and floats in the sea. Also used figuratively in the expression 'tip of the iceberg.'

examples.japanese: {氷山|ひょうざん}の{一角|いっかく}にすぎない。
examples.english: It is only the tip of the iceberg.

examples.japanese: {大|おお}きな{氷山|ひょうざん}が{海|うみ}に{浮|う}かんでいた。
examples.english: A large iceberg was floating in the sea.

examples.japanese: この{問題|もんだい}は{氷山|ひょうざん}の{一角|いっかく}で、{実際|じっさい}にはもっと{深刻|しんこく}な{状況|じょうきょう}だ。
examples.english: This problem is just the tip of the iceberg — the actual situation is much more serious.

notes:
USAGE:
Most commonly encountered in the set phrase {氷山|ひょうざん}の{一角|いっかく} (the tip of the iceberg), meaning that what is visible represents only a small portion of a larger problem or situation. This expression parallels the English idiom exactly.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {氷山|ひょうざん}の{一角|いっかく} (tip of the iceberg)
- {氷山|ひょうざん}が{浮|う}かぶ (an iceberg floats)
- {氷山|ひょうざん}にぶつかる (to collide with an iceberg)
